14	CASE OD2-HO-KNOWN-1 (KNOWN, technical): Android login success drop at Oxleigh Mutual
15	Setting: Oxleigh Mutual is a fictional mid-sized retail bank with about 1.2 million mobile-app customers. Its Android and iOS apps call a mobile API that sits behind a vendor-managed edge protection service supplied by Corvane. Customers log in either by typing a password or by biometric/PIN quick-unlock on a device they have already enrolled. A product analytics team reports login success rates from in-app telemetry.
16	Presenting request: The Head of Digital Channels asks why Android login success has dropped since 3 March and what the bank should do now. She expects a rollback plan for Android release 6.14 by Thursday.
17	INITIAL EVIDENCE
18	E1 [stage S1] Email from Priya Lindqvist, Head of Digital Channels, 10 March (leadership-account): Team — Android login success has fallen off a cliff. Seven-day average was 97.1% for 24 Feb–2 Mar and 88.7% for 3–9 Mar. iOS is flat (97.4% to 97.3%) and web is flat (96.8% to 96.9%). The Android store rating for this week is 3.1, down from 4.4. Android 6.14 started rolling out on 3 March with the new password screen, and the timing speaks for itself. I want a rollback plan on my desk by Thursday and a clear explanation for the executive committee. Please don't spend a week on analysis; customers are locked out now.
19	E2 [stage S1] Notes from Tomás Reyes, Android engineering lead, 9 March (manager-account): 6.14 staged rollout began 3 Mar 09:00 UTC via the store console. Changes: redesigned password-login screen; our networking library nettle-http bumped from 4.11 to 4.12 (the Android app uses nettle-http for every API call); new analytics events. Crash-free sessions unchanged. The extra failures seem to be in password logins; biometric/PIN quick-unlock looks normal. We could not reproduce on our test devices against staging. Worth noting the March Android security patch started reaching phones around 2 March, and in 2024 an OS update broke keystore-backed login for us for two weeks. Can't rule either out yet.
20	E3 [stage S1] Change calendar extract, production, 2–4 March (change-record): CHG-5521 | 2 Mar 22:00 UTC | Core banking database index maintenance. Closed, no incidents.
21	CHG-5530 | 3 Mar 09:00 UTC | Android app 6.14 staged rollout start (store console). Owner: Mobile.
22	CHG-5534 | 3 Mar, vendor window | Edge protection (Corvane): vendor-managed rule pack auto-update to 2026.03.1. Standard change, pre-approved, applied by vendor; no bank testing required.
23	CHG-5536 | 3 Mar 14:00 UTC | Auth service: session-token lifetime for all mobile client IDs (iOS and Android) reduced from 30 to 20 minutes. Affects session expiry only.
24	CHG-5540 | 4 Mar 08:00 UTC | Marketing website TLS certificate renewal.
25	E4 [stage S1] Message from Dana Okafor, Security Operations manager, 9 March (manager-account): On 28 Feb we stopped a credential-stuffing run against web login. My read is that the Android drop is the same crowd moving onto the mobile API: bots fail logins, the success rate goes down. Two asks: (1) exclude edge-blocked attempts from the login KPI, because those are not real customers and they are distorting the number executives see; (2) raise Corvane bot-protection sensitivity on all login endpoints from 'standard' to 'high' until this blows over. Happy to brief the executive committee.
26	E5 [stage S1] Digital analytics KPI definition: mobile login success rate (v3, January) (document): Login success rate = login-success events ÷ login-attempt events, both emitted by the in-app telemetry SDK. An attempt event is emitted when a user submits a password or triggers biometric/PIN quick-unlock in an installed copy of the app. Each event carries an app-install ID, app version, OS version and an outcome category: success, credentials rejected, request rejected by server, or network/timeout. Requests sent to the API by scripts or tools other than the installed app do not emit telemetry events and are not counted. Dashboard tiles show the platform-level rate only.
27	E6 [stage S1] Contact-centre weekly operations summary, week of 2 March (system-record): Inbound calls 2–8 March: 41,200 against a four-week average of 34,900 (+18%). Average wait 6m40s (target 3m). Scheduled events this week: annual account-fee notices mailed 2 March to 610,000 customers; savings-rate change emailed 4 March. Reason coding: 57% of calls logged as 'General enquiry', the default code; a January coding audit found reason codes unreliable for trend analysis. Team leads report 'a mix of fee questions and people who can't get into the app'.
28	CATALOGUE (full contents)
29	C1 [stage S1] Android login outcomes by app version, OS version and outcome category, 24 Feb–9 Mar - Product analytics, in-app telemetry extract (telemetry): Daily averages; pre = 24 Feb–2 Mar, post = 4–9 Mar. Quick-unlock: 96,700 → 96,900 attempts/day, success 97.2% → 97.2%. Password: 7,500 → 10,600 attempts/day, success 96.0% → 8.2%. Overall 97.1% → 88.4%. Post success by app version (share of attempts): 6.11 and older 88.3% (6%); 6.12 88.6% (18%); 6.13 88.4% (71%); 6.14 88.5% (5%; staged rollout at 5%, 10% from 6 Mar). Pre: 6.12 97.0%, 6.13 97.1%. Post by OS: Android 11 to 15 all between 88.2% and 88.6%; March security patch installed 88.4%, not installed 88.4%. Added failures are all 'request rejected by server' (HTTP 403) on password submissions, first logged 3 Mar 10:41 UTC on every version within one minute. Before 10:41, 6.14 logged 38 password attempts (1 credentials rejected); afterwards few password submissions reach a credential decision, so credential-error rates cannot be compared.
30	C2 [stage S1] Corvane edge event log export, mobile API authentication paths, 1–9 March - Corvane tenant console export pulled by bank platform team (log): Tenant: Oxleigh mobile API. Rule pack 2026.03.1 activated 3 Mar 10:38 UTC. New rule AUTO-LIB-17 'automation HTTP library user-agent on authentication path': matches user-agent 'nettle-http' AND path /auth/password/* AND no edge session cookie; action block (HTTP 403, vendor HTML page). AUTO-LIB-17 blocks: 1–2 Mar none (rule absent); 3 Mar 6,050, first at 10:41; 4–9 Mar 9,580–9,840 per day. Blocked requests carried header X-Client: oxleigh-android and an app-install ID: 41,300 distinct install IDs, 92% with a successful login from the same install ID in the prior 90 days; mean 1.6 blocked requests per install ID over the week, maximum 14. AUTO-LIB-17 hits on iOS (user-agent 'OxleighGo-iOS/5.21'), web, or quick-unlock path /auth/device-token: 0. Forwarded Android password requests: origin returned 401 for 1.9% and 5xx for 0.1%, unchanged from before 3 Mar.
31	C3 [stage S1] Android 6.14 release notes and merged change list - Mobile engineering release record (document): Release 6.14 (build 61400), approved 27 Feb. User-facing: redesigned password-login screen (larger fields, show-password toggle, inline error messages); updated card-freeze flow wording. Technical: nettle-http 4.11.3 → 4.12.0 (connection-pool fixes); analytics SDK events for screen timings; minimum Android version unchanged at 11. 214 merged changes, 9 touching login code, all in the password-screen UI layer. Regression suite: 1,140 automated tests passed on staging. Sign-off: Mobile engineering lead, QA lead, Product owner.

Top crash clusters unchanged: image-cache out-of-memory on low-memory devices, push-token refresh race. No crash cluster references login, the password screen or nettle-http. iOS crash-free sessions 99.71% → 99.70% over the same periods.
33	C5 [stage S1] Authentication service outcome summary, 1–9 March - Backend platform team, auth-service log summary (log): All channels combined; this summary is not broken down by platform or client. 34	C6 [stage S1] Corvane support ticket response, 9 March - Corvane customer support, ticket CS-77812 (vendor-account): Thank you for your enquiry. We have no indication that the update affects legitimate mobile application traffic, and we recommend investigating recent client releases. Please reopen this ticket with request samples if the issue persists.

Recommendations: keep rate limits as configured; review bot-protection posture in Q2. The same actor could retarget other channels in future, and this cannot be excluded.
36	C8 [stage S1] Contact-centre reason-code report and coding audit, 2–9 March - Contact-centre quality team (system-record): Calls by reason code against four-week average: General enquiry +3,700; Fees and charges +1,400; Digital access +900; Cards +300. Auditor's note: the sample is too small and platform capture too inconsistent to apportion the weekly rise between causes.
37	C9 [stage S1] App store ratings and review sample, Android and iOS, 1–9 March - Store console exports (customer-account): Android: 1,860 new ratings, weekly average 3.1 (prior week 4.4). Sample of 40 one- and two-star reviews: 31 mention password login failing with 'Something went wrong, please try again'; 6 say fingerprint login still works; 3 unrelated. iOS: 1,240 new ratings, average 4.5 (prior week 4.5). Representative Android review: 'Changed my phone so I have to use my password now and it just won't let me in. Called the bank, waited 40 minutes.'
38	C10 [stage S1] Interview with Mei Sørensen, QA lead, on 6.14 test coverage, 10 March - Interview notes (staff-account): '6.14 went through the full login regression suite on 20 physical devices, Android 11 through 15. 39	C11 [stage S1] Mobile API availability and latency dashboard, 1–9 March - Platform operations monitoring (telemetry): Availability (non-5xx responses ÷ all responses at origin): 99.97% in both weeks. p95 latency 210 ms → 214 ms. Edge-handled responses (bot challenges and blocks) are excluded from availability by design; they are counted as 'protected' rather than failed. No availability or latency alerts fired 1–9 March. The per-endpoint panel for the password-login path shows origin latency only.
40	C12 [stage S1] iOS login outcomes by app version, 24 Feb–9 Mar - Product analytics, in-app telemetry extract (telemetry): Overall iOS login success 97.4% pre (24 Feb–2 Mar) and 97.3% post (4–9 Mar). No iOS release since 18 February. Outcome categories unchanged; 'request rejected by server' 0.1% in both periods.
41	C13 [stage S1] On-call engineering chat transcript, 3–4 March - Engineering on-call channel export (staff-account): 3 Mar 13:52 [Ivo, backend on-call]: seeing a bump in Android login failures on the dashboard, auth service looks healthy.
42	3 Mar 14:20 [Ivo]: token lifetime change just went out, could that be related?
43	3 Mar 15:05 [Rhea, mobile]: will look at 6.14 crash data.
44	4 Mar 09:12 [Ivo]: still elevated, nothing odd in auth logs. Parking until Mobile confirms.
45	4 Mar 09:30 [Rhea]: can't reproduce on staging. Escalating to Tomás.
46	C14 [stage S1] Sample of customer complaint emails tagged 'login', 4–8 March - Customer complaints team (customer-account): Sample of 25 emails tagged 'login': 19 from Android users, 4 iOS, 2 web. Typical Android text: 'Every time I put my password in I get Something went wrong (ref S-403). Fingerprint works on my tablet but my new phone needs the password.' Five Android complainants say they reinstalled the app; none say it helped. The iOS emails concern forgotten passwords; both web emails are about the fee notice.
47	C15 [stage S1] Third-party service status pages (analytics SDK, push notifications, SMS passcodes, maps), 1–9 March - Vendor public status page archives (external-data): Analytics SDK provider: operational, no incidents. Push provider: 'degraded delivery in EU region' 5 Mar 02:00–03:10 UTC, resolved. SMS passcode provider: operational; one incident 'delayed delivery to one carrier' 7 Mar 18:00–18:40 UTC. Maps SDK: operational. None of the listed incidents spans 3 March. Oxleigh uses SMS passcodes only for new-device enrolment, on both iOS and Android.
48	CANDIDATES
49	H1: A defect introduced in Android app release 6.14 is causing the drop in Android login success.
50	H2: A change in the edge protection layer in front of the mobile API is rejecting legitimate Android login requests, causing the drop in Android login success.
51	H3: Automated credential-stuffing traffic is pulling down the measured Android login success rate.
52	H4: A recent Android operating-system security update on customers' phones is causing Android login attempts to fail.
53	H5: The redesigned password screen in release 6.14 makes customers enter wrong credentials more often.
54	H6: The 3 March change to the authentication service is rejecting valid Android login requests.
55	R1: 3 March vendor rule-pack update to the edge protection layer -> Drop in Android login success from 3 March (causes)
56	R2: Rollout of Android release 6.14 -> Drop in Android login success from 3 March (causes)
57	R3: Drop in Android login success from 3 March -> 18% rise in contact-centre call volume, week of 2 March (causes)
58	R4: Credential-stuffing activity against Oxleigh's login services -> Drop in Android login success from 3 March (causes)
59	A1: Have the edge vendor set the rules added in the 3 March rule-pack update to log-only on the mobile password-login path, keeping rate limits, account lockout and all other edge rules active, then confirm in telemetry that Android password-login success returns to its pre-3 March level.
60	A2: Raise edge bot-protection sensitivity on all login endpoints from 'standard' to 'high' until the suspected credential-stuffing subsides.
61	A3: Exclude edge-blocked login attempts from the login success KPI reported to executives, treating them as non-customer traffic.
62	A4: Continue the Android 6.14 staged rollout on its planned schedule while tracking login outcomes by app version.
63	A5: Revert the redesigned password screen in the next Android release.

Recommendations: keep rate limits as configured; review bot-protection posture in Q2. The same actor could retarget other channels in future, and this cannot be excluded.
C8 [stage S1] Contact-centre reason-code report and coding audit, 2–9 March - Contact-centre quality team (system-record): Calls by reason code against four-week average: General enquiry +3,700; Fees and charges +1,400; Digital access +900; Cards +300. Audit of 200 sampled 'General enquiry' recordings from 4–6 March: 61 about fee notices, 38 about app or online-banking access (platform recorded in only 9 of these), 101 other or unclassifiable. Auditor's note: the sample is too small and platform capture too inconsistent to apportion the weekly rise between causes.
C9 [stage S1] App store ratings and review sample, Android and iOS, 1–9 March - Store console exports (customer-account): Android: 1,860 new ratings, weekly average 3.1 (prior week 4.4). Sample of 40 one- and two-star reviews: 31 mention password login failing with 'Something went wrong, please try again'; 6 say fingerprint login still works; 3 unrelated. iOS: 1,240 new ratings, average 4.5 (prior week 4.5). Representative Android review: 'Changed my phone so I have to use my password now and it just won't let me in. Called the bank, waited 40 minutes.'
C10 [stage S1] Interview with Mei Sørensen, QA lead, on 6.14 test coverage, 10 March - Interview notes (staff-account): '6.14 went through the full login regression suite on 20 physical devices, Android 11 through 15. Everything passed. Our test devices point at the staging API, and staging doesn't have the Corvane layer in front of it; it goes straight to the load balancer. When the drop started I re-ran password login on 6.13 and 6.14 against staging and both were fine. I can't test against production without real customer credentials, which we're not allowed to use.'
C11 [stage S1] Mobile API availability and latency dashboard, 1–9 March - Platform operations monitoring (telemetry): Availability (non-5xx responses ÷ all responses at origin): 99.97% in both weeks. p95 latency 210 ms → 214 ms. Edge-handled responses (bot challenges and blocks) are excluded from availability by design; they are counted as 'protected' rather than failed. No availability or latency alerts fired 1–9 March. The per-endpoint panel for the password-login path shows origin latency only.
C12 [stage S1] iOS login outcomes by app version, 24 Feb–9 Mar - Product analytics, in-app telemetry extract (telemetry): Overall iOS login success 97.4% pre (24 Feb–2 Mar) and 97.3% post (4–9 Mar). Password: 5,900 → 6,000 attempts/day, success 96.3% → 96.2%. Quick-unlock: 88,400 → 88,700 attempts/day, success 97.5% → 97.4%. Post success by version: 5.20 97.3%, 5.21 97.3%. No iOS release since 18 February. Outcome categories unchanged; 'request rejected by server' 0.1% in both periods.
C13 [stage S1] On-call engineering chat transcript, 3–4 March - Engineering on-call channel export (staff-account): 3 Mar 13:52 [Ivo, backend on-call]: seeing a bump in Android login failures on the dashboard, auth service looks healthy.
3 Mar 14:20 [Ivo]: token lifetime change just went out, could that be related?
3 Mar 15:05 [Rhea, mobile]: will look at 6.14 crash data.
4 Mar 09:12 [Ivo]: still elevated, nothing odd in auth logs. Parking until Mobile confirms.
4 Mar 09:30 [Rhea]: can't reproduce on staging. Escalating to Tomás.
C14 [stage S1] Sample of customer complaint emails tagged 'login', 4–8 March - Customer complaints team (customer-account): Sample of 25 emails tagged 'login': 19 from Android users, 4 iOS, 2 web. Typical Android text: 'Every time I put my password in I get Something went wrong (ref S-403). Fingerprint works on my tablet but my new phone needs the password.' Five Android complainants say they reinstalled the app; none say it helped. The iOS emails concern forgotten passwords; both web emails are about the fee notice.
C15 [stage S1] Third-party service status pages (analytics SDK, push notifications, SMS passcodes, maps), 1–9 March - Vendor public status page archives (external-data): Analytics SDK provider: operational, no incidents. Push provider: 'degraded delivery in EU region' 5 Mar 02:00–03:10 UTC, resolved. SMS passcode provider: operational; one incident 'delayed delivery to one carrier' 7 Mar 18:00–18:40 UTC. Maps SDK: operational. None of the listed incidents spans 3 March. Oxleigh uses SMS passcodes only for new-device enrolment, on both iOS and Android.
CANDIDATES
H1: A defect introduced in Android app release 6.14 is causing the drop in Android login success.
H2: A change in the edge protection layer in front of the mobile API is rejecting legitimate Android login requests, causing the drop in Android login success.
H3: Automated credential-stuffing traffic is pulling down the measured Android login success rate.
H4: A recent Android operating-system security update on customers' phones is causing Android login attempts to fail.
H5: The redesigned password screen in release 6.14 makes customers enter wrong credentials more often.
H6: The 3 March change to the authentication service is rejecting valid Android login requests.
R1: 3 March vendor rule-pack update to the edge protection layer -> Drop in Android login success from 3 March (causes)
R2: Rollout of Android release 6.14 -> Drop in Android login success from 3 March (causes)
R3: Drop in Android login success from 3 March -> 18% rise in contact-centre call volume, week of 2 March (causes)
R4: Credential-stuffing activity against Oxleigh's login services -> Drop in Android login success from 3 March (causes)
A1: Have the edge vendor set the rules added in the 3 March rule-pack update to log-only on the mobile password-login path, keeping rate limits, account lockout and all other edge rules active, then confirm in telemetry that Android password-login success returns to its pre-3 March level.
A2: Raise edge bot-protection sensitivity on all login endpoints from 'standard' to 'high' until the suspected credential-stuffing subsides.
A3: Exclude edge-blocked login attempts from the login success KPI reported to executives, treating them as non-customer traffic.
A4: Continue the Android 6.14 staged rollout on its planned schedule while tracking login outcomes by app version.
A5: Revert the redesigned password screen in the next Android release.

answers.justification: C1 shows the same post-3 March success rate (about 88.4%) on every app version, including 6.11 and older, 6.12 and 6.13, while 6.14 made up only 5% of attempts. C4 shows no login-related crash cluster, and C3/C10 show 6.14 passed the regression suite.

In C2, rule pack 2026.03.1 went live at 10:38 and new rule AUTO-LIB-17 blocked nettle-http password requests from 10:41, the same minute failures began in C1. About 9,700 blocks a day matches the added 403 failures in C1, and 92% of blocked installs had logged in successfully before. iOS and quick-unlock had zero hits (C2, C12), and origin outcomes are unchanged (C2, C5).

E5 says script traffic sends no telemetry and is not counted in the KPI. The blocked requests came from 41,300 real app installs, 92% with earlier successful logins (C2). C7 found mobile traffic normal during the 28 February web attack.

C1 shows identical post-period success (88.4%) whether or not the March security patch is installed, and Android 11–15 all fall between 88.2% and 88.6%. Quick-unlock, which would depend on the keystore, is unchanged.

The added failures are server 403s, not credential rejections (C1). The origin 401 rate for forwarded Android password requests is unchanged at 1.9% (C2, C5), and the drop is identical on versions without the new screen (C1).

Failures began at 10:41 (C1, C2), before the 14:00 token change (E3). The token change applied to iOS too, yet iOS is flat (C12). Auth-service outcomes are unchanged (C5), and the rejections come from the edge, not the origin (C2).

The timing fits (rule activated 10:38, first failure 10:41), there is a clear mechanism (AUTO-LIB-17 matches the app's nettle-http user-agent on the password path; C2, E2), and block counts match the added failures (C1, C2). Rivals are ruled out: app version, OS (C1), auth service (C5) and other platforms (C12).
C1 shows the drop on all versions at once within one minute and at equal size, while 6.14 accounted for only 5% of attempts; before 10:41, 6.14 password logins were normal.

Calls rose in the same week, and some calls, reviews and complaints mention app access (E6, C8, C9, C14). But fee notices to 610,000 customers are a major confounder, and the C8 auditor says the rise cannot be split between causes.
Bot traffic is excluded from the telemetry KPI (E5). The blocked traffic comes from genuine installs (C2), and mobile traffic was normal during the stuffing event (C7).
This is a targeted, reversible fix aimed at the cause shown in C2/C1. It keeps rate limits and lockout (C7) in place and has a built-in telemetry check that also tests the causal claim.
Raising sensitivity would probably block even more legitimate app traffic, given C2 shows the edge already blocking real customers. Its premise (H3) is contradicted by E5, C2 and C7.
The edge-blocked attempts are real customers (C2: 92% with earlier successful logins). Excluding them would hide the outage from executives, and C11 already hides edge blocks from availability.
6.14 is not the cause (C1, C3, C4), so continuing the staged rollout with per-version tracking is reasonable, though it does nothing to fix the edge problem.

Reverting the screen does nothing for the real cause. H5 is contradicted by unchanged origin 401 rates (C2) and an identical drop on older versions (C1), so this action is unjustified; 'premature' is the nearest allowed label.
C1, C2, C5 and C12 together pin the cause on AUTO-LIB-17 strongly enough to commit to A1. A1 is targeted, reversible and self-verifying.

ambiguousItems: Q-A5: none of the allowed labels fits an action that rests on a contradicted hypothesis but does no real damage. 'premature' assumes the hypothesis is still unconfirmed, and 'harmful' needs real damage; either could be argued.
Q-A4: 'acceptable' versus 'preferred'. Continuing the rollout rightly rejects the requested rollback, but it is not the fix.
Q-R3: 'association-only' versus 'unknown'. The fee-notice confounder and unreliable reason coding (E6, C8) weaken even the association.
caseProblems: E1 reports post-period Android success as 88.7% for 3–9 March; C1 reports 88.4% for 4–9 March. The windows differ, so this is consistent, but the mismatch may confuse solvers.
C2 states the user-agent and rule match so precisely that a single item nearly settles H2. That is realistic for a vendor log, but the case becomes easy once C2 is read.

C2 gives a mean of 1.6 blocked requests per install over the week, which is low next to complaints that say 'every time' (C14) and the higher password retry volume (C1). It is plausible if users switch to quick-unlock or give up.
The A5 label set has no option for an action that is simply not indicated.
